title: Mid-Year Family Law Check-In: Does Your Parenting Plan Still Work?

content.rendered:
Reviewing your parenting plan in Colorado can help you determine whether your current arrangements still meet your family’s needs.

Life changes quickly, and family law orders that once worked well may no longer fit your family’s current circumstances.

Why Reviewing Your Parenting Plan in Colorado Is Important

Family law orders are based on circumstances at a specific point in time. Over the course of a year, many factors can change, including employment, finances, children’s schedules, and living arrangements.

Reviewing your orders periodically can help:

  • Ensure parenting schedules still meet your children’s needs.
    • Address changes in income that may affect child support.
    • Prevent misunderstandings between co-parents.
    • Identify potential legal issues before they escalate.
    • Keep court orders aligned with your family’s current situation.

Taking a proactive approach can save time, reduce conflict, and provide greater stability for everyone involved.

Has Your Ex’s Income Changed?

A significant change in income may affect child support obligations.

Consider whether:

  • Has either party received a promotion or pay increase.
    • Has either party experienced a job loss or reduction in hours.
    • Has either party’s financial circumstances substantially changed.
    • Has either party’s income has changed significantly.

Colorado law allows child support modifications in certain situations when there has been a substantial and continuing change in circumstances.

Have Your Children’s Schedules Changed?

Children’s needs often evolve throughout the year. New school schedules, extracurricular activities, sports, and social commitments may create challenges under an existing parenting plan.

Ask yourself:

  • Are parenting exchanges still working smoothly?
    • Have school or activity schedules changed?
    • Are transportation arrangements creating difficulties?
    • Does your child need more flexibility as they get older?

Making adjustments when necessary can help reduce stress for both parents and children.

Are You Experiencing Co-Parenting Challenges?

Even when parenting plans are well-written, conflicts can arise over time.

Common issues include:

  • Communication difficulties between parents.
    • Disagreements regarding schedules.
    • Decision-making conflicts.
    • Missed parenting time.
    • Ongoing disputes about responsibilities.

Addressing concerns early can often help prevent more serious disputes in the future.

Are Relocation or Travel Plans Affecting Your Family?

Summer often brings travel opportunities, job changes, and potential relocations.

Parents should consider:

  • Whether upcoming travel plans require coordination.
    • If relocation may impact parenting time.
    • Whether transportation arrangements remain practical.
    • If additional provisions are needed for long-distance parenting.

Certain moves may require court approval or modifications to existing orders, making early planning especially important.

Do Your Current Orders Still Reflect Your Family’s Needs?

The most important question is whether your current court orders continue to serve your family’s best interests.

Consider:

  • Are your children thriving under the current arrangement?
    • Is the parenting schedule realistic?
    • Are child support obligations appropriate?
    • Have circumstances changed since the orders were entered?
    • Would modifications improve stability for your family?

A periodic review can help ensure your orders continue to support your family’s long-term success.
